title: Enteral feeding

sources.use: NHS patient safety alert on nasogastric tube misplacement

objectives: Confirm tube position before each use.

items.text: ESICM 2017 favours early enteral nutrition over delayed enteral or parenteral nutrition in critically ill adults who can be fed enterally (mostly conditional recommendations, many based on expert opinion).

Confirm nasogastric position after placement and before each use by the approved clinical pathway (NICE CG32: aspirate with pH-graded paper, X-ray if necessary). A stable external tube-length marker alone does not establish safe *initial* placement; markers are an adjunct when checking a previously verified tube. Never flush, give medicines, water or feed through a tube whose position is unconfirmed. Where aspiration or pH assessment is unreliable, escalate and use an approved alternative rather than assuming placement.
Introducing fluids or medicines into the respiratory tract or pleura through a misplaced tube is a Never Event in England (NHS 2016 alert).
Keep the head of the bed raised unless contraindicated (SHEA 2022 essential practice).
Insert and check tubes only with the relevant skills and training (NICE CG32).
Whether the unit measures gastric aspirates, at what interval and with what thresholds, and who may place tubes, is local policy.
Feeding product, pump and tube type follow unit supplies and manufacturer instructions.

For nasogastric feeds, NICE CG32 recommendation 1.7.17 calls for position confirmation after insertion and before each use by aspirate with pH-graded paper (with X-ray when necessary). Its monitoring table also discusses checking tube markers after initial position confirmation; external marks help detect migration but must not be mistaken for an independent initial-position test. For repeat use, follow the unit's approved risk-based confirmation pathway. If displacement or aspiration is suspected, or position is uncertain, withhold feed, water and medication until placement is confirmed by an approved method.
Feed start, rate changes, flushing and medicine administration via tubes: not covered by the sources read; follow the dietitian's plan and unit procedure.
Tube position and fixation, feed tolerance, aspiration signs, head-of-bed angle.
Stop the feed and escalate if tube position cannot be confirmed or the patient shows respiratory distress after feeding starts.
Record position check method and result, feed type and rate, tolerance and escalation per your unit's documentation standard.

checklist.text: Confirm tube position by the unit's approved method before each use; do not feed if it cannot be confirmed.
Perform hand hygiene and check the feed order.
Raise the head of the bed unless contraindicated.
Check tube fixation, nasal skin and that the tube is intact, unblocked and unkinked daily.
Stop the feed and escalate for suspected misplacement or respiratory distress.
Record the position check, feed and tolerance.

gaps: Energy and protein targets, parenteral nutrition, refeeding, medicine administration via tubes: not covered.
Non-UK placement verification methods (ultrasound, electromagnetic): not read.
ASPEN and ESPEN guidelines: not accessed.
